children: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on Wednesday closed adjudication proceedings against Lloyds Enterprises (LEL), its Managing Director Rajesh Rajnarayan Gupta and Chief Financial Officer Viresh Shankar Sohoni, following a settlement with the market regulator.

In an order dated November 25, SEBI said the proceedings had come to an end without examining the merits of the allegations. This means the regulator did not decide whether the company or its executives were guilty of the alleged violations. The closure follows a settlement order passed by SEBI on September 29, 2026.
A decade-long trail of interest-free loans
The case began after the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) sent an alert to SEBI in November 2023, flagging possible irregularities in the financial advances reported by Lloyds Enterprises.

SEBI's investigation found that the company had transferred ₹144.82 crore to two entities — Cheerful Trade & Realty Developers and Triumph Trade & Properties Developers — during the 2006–07 financial year.

According to SEBI, the money was given without charging any interest and without signing formal agreements. The regulator alleged that the advances benefited the company's promoters and entities linked to them. The funds remained misutilised until the 2022–23 financial year.

SEBI also alleged that Lloyds Enterprises did not account for possible losses on these advances between 2016–17 and 2020–21, as required under Indian Accounting Standard (Ind AS) 109. In simple terms, the company did not make the necessary provisions for money that it might not recover. This allegedly led to its financial statements showing a higher value than they should have.

SEBI's investigation also found that the two companies receiving the advances were related parties of Lloyds Enterprises. This means they had links to the company or its promoters and should have been disclosed as such in its annual reports.
However, Lloyds Enterprises allegedly did not disclose these relationships between 2016–17 and 2022–23, as required under SEBI's Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR) Regulations.

The investigation further found that Lloyds Enterprises eventually received a 7% partnership interest in Lloyds Metals & Minerals Trading Limited Liability Partnership in exchange for the ₹144.82 crore advances. The partnership had a net worth of ₹5,852.64 crore at the time.
SEBI issued a show-cause notice to the company and its executives in July 2025, alleging violations of listing rules and regulations aimed at preventing fraudulent and unfair trade practices.
After the company and the executives settled the matter with SEBI in September 2026, the regulator has now formally closed the adjudication proceedings.
Shares of Lloyds Enterprises closed at ₹60.51 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on Wednesday, down 1.67%, ahead of SEBI's announcement.

title: SEBI closes proceedings against Lloyds Enterprises, executives after settlement
